extractions.value: At presentation, she fulfilled clinical criteria for SPS (1, 2). She did not have Babinski signs. Supportive evidence for this diagnosis was the absence of lumbar lordosis in plain radiographs of the spine early in the course, the collapse of L4 and L2 vertebrae (thought to have been the result of lumbar paraspinal muscle spasms), and the presence of chronic inflammatory cells in the pancreas (some associated with islets) consistent with a reaction to anti-islet cell antibodies.

extractions.value: Patient had subacute encephalomyelitis confirmed at autopsy, presenting as SPS. She developed paroxysmal leg jerking and apnea spells 2.5 years after SPS onset. Autopsy showed diffuse encephalomyelitis with perivascular cuffing in spinal cord, brainstem, thalamus, hippocampus, and amygdala, and dense mononuclear infiltrate in anterior horns of lumbar and cervical cord.
extractions.quote: Autopsy showed small chronic inflammatory foci in the pancreas (some associated with islets) and findings of diffuse encephalomyelitis characterized by perivascular cuffing in the spinal cord, brainstem, thalamus, hippocampus, and amygdala
